english.title: Sponsor fail to ensure suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions in 3rd country site entered in European database

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial being conducted at a trial site in a third country, namely **(..SPECIFY THE COUNTRY..), in addition to sites in the United Kingdom, failed to ensure that all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions occurring at that site were entered into the European database established in accordance with Article 11 of Directive 2001/20/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 34, 49(1)(i) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 49 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 makes a breach of reg 34 an offence.
(ii) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides that a person does not commit an offence under these Regulations if he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of that offence. Where evidence is adduced which is sufficient to raise an issue with respect to that defence, the court or jury shall assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.
(iii) The legislation was amended as a result of the EU Exit. For offences from 1st January 2021, see H20246.
